info.name: Alpen API
info.description:
Alpen Wege API (generated by build_postman.py from the API's OpenAPI description).

**Use:** import this collection and `Alpen API local.postman_environment.json`, select the environment, run **profile / auth / Login admin** once, then any call. Tokens last only a few minutes; the collection keeps the newest one automatically (header `X-Access-Token`). If a call answers 401, log in again.

**URL:** `http://{{hostname}}:{{port}}/{{api_path}}/<app>/<resource>`. Folders: one per app (core, assets, compendium, explorer, profile, management), one per model inside.

**Photos and GPX files (assets):** run **assets / photos / Upload photo** once. It saves `photo_id`, and from then on the Create and Update calls of cards, POIs and posts send `"main_photo_id": "{{photo_id}}"`, so they all use that photo (an empty `photo_id` is filled with the first photo of the list; when there is no photo at all the field is left out). **explorer / tracks / Upload track** saves `gpx_id`, the stored file shown in assets / gpx. The upload requests point at `sample_photo.jpg` and `sample_track.gpx`: put both files in the Postman working directory (Settings, General, Working directory) or choose a file in the body once.

**Icons and flags (assets):** run **assets / icons / Upload icon** once (admin). It saves `icon_id` and `icon_key`, and from then on the Create and Update calls of the 19 reference tables, resource types, countries and regions send `"icon_id": "{{icon_id}}"`, so they all use that icon (an empty `icon_id` is filled with the first icon of the list, for example a flag; when there is no icon at all the field is left out). `assets / icons / Icon file ...` shows the picture (SVG, PNG, by id or by key). **All icons at once:** `Upload icons CSV (dry run)`, then `Upload icons CSV (import all)` (the CSV `icons_import.csv` carries the graphics of all 438 icons; with `link=true` countries and regions get their flag), and `Link rows to icons by key` for later. Reference values and resource types need an icon: on an empty database upload one before the core folder. The upload requests point at `sample_icon.svg` and `icons_import.csv`: put both in the Postman working directory too.

**Variables:** `hostname`, `port`, `api_path` (= `api/v1`), `<who>_email` / `<who>_password` for admin, editor, viewer, guest, `new_user_password`, and `access_token`. Create calls save ids in variables such as `country_id`, `region_id`, `poi_id`; the next calls use them. **Run a single request alone:** run **Collect first IDs (optional) / Collect first IDs (all lists)** once (after a login), or any List request: they save the id of the first row in the variable of each model. Get one, Update and Delete requests also fill an empty variable themselves from the first row of their list. Careful: a Delete request with such an id deletes a real row. For a full run with the Collection Runner: set `skip_deletes` to `true` (the Delete calls of the model folders are skipped), run the app folders in the order shown, then run the folder **Cleanup (optional)**, which deletes everything in the right order. The Upload CSV and Upload track calls need a file chosen in their body.

**Not covered:** WebSocket requests (see management / ws for the ticket and the URLs).

request.description:
The card as printed. The picture is the main photo of the card; a card without its own photo uses the main photo of its POI.

Query parameters (the two switched on are the defaults; tick the others to try them, each has an example value):
- `format`: json (every value on the card, translated), svg, png, jpg or pdf (print, 3 mm bleed). Default svg.
- `lang`: en, de or pl, the language of every text on the card. A text empty in that language comes from the next one (en, de, pl).
- `ratio`: shape as width:height, whole numbers 1 to 100, between 2:5 and 5:2. Default 63:88 (trading card); also 1:1, 4:5, 9:16, 3:2, 16:9. The shorter side is always 63 mm. From 13:10 on the photo moves to the left of the texts.
- `style`: look of the card, `standard` (default) or `3d` (raised frame, glass panels, holographic sheen). Another name answers 422.
- `dpi`: sharpness of a png or jpg, 72 to 2000, default 300 (815 x 1110 px on 63:88; 600 gives twice the width and height). The jpg records it. Wide or tall shapes have more pixels, so very high values answer 422 with the highest dpi that fits (63:88 up to 2000, 16:9 up to 1990, 5:2 up to 1690). Ignored for svg, pdf and json.
- `download`: true saves the file instead of showing it.

Only 63:88, standard style, 300 dpi is stored by the render job and served from disk when up to date; everything else is drawn on request (a 2000 dpi picture takes several seconds).
